evidence: Scroll progress timelines are distinct from time-driven triggers and may be sampled asynchronously without running script for each scroll update.
testable_application: A/B CSS scroll timelines for DOM-only copy/theme transforms while retaining JS for the 3D rig.

evidence: requestAnimationFrame schedules one animation resampling callback; subsequent frames require another request.
testable_application: Use one frame authority to sample progress and derive all visible 3D state.

evidence: rAF generally follows display refresh and is paused in hidden contexts; 120 and 144 Hz displays are common.
testable_application: Measure idle rAF interval distribution and label the actual environment before applying an 8.33 ms gate.

evidence: Input, tasks, rAF, style/layout, and rendering share a per-refresh event-loop budget.
testable_application: Capture frame intervals and root-cause traces for the same repeatable scroll.

evidence: LoAF exposes frames at least 50 ms and attributes script, render, style, and layout timing.
testable_application: Add PerformanceObserver LoAF telemetry with long-task fallback; use it for cause, not the 120 Hz threshold.

evidence: Presentation delay extends from event callback completion until the next paint; INP measures responsiveness across interactions.
testable_application: Keep nonvisual work outside active input/scroll and record event-to-next-paint separately from frame cadence.

evidence: scheduler.yield can split long tasks and allow pending high-priority work before continuation.
testable_application: Use only for chunkable post-load work such as noncritical preparation; do not yield inside per-frame pose math.

evidence: Mismatched input and display frequencies can create visible jitter even when individual components work correctly.
testable_application: Measure pose delta conditional on progress delta and keep one sampled progress value per frame.

evidence: Frequent 4–12 ms frame-time variations affect perceived smoothness across 30–240 Hz conditions.
testable_application: Track interval variance and miss streaks, not only mean FPS.

evidence: Synchronous queries, compile checks, uploads, and high backing-store cost can stall or increase mobile bandwidth pressure.
testable_application: Avoid per-frame GL queries; capture renderer statistics once per phase; A/B DPR and MSAA.

evidence: KTX2 supports universal textures, supercompression, mip levels, and efficient GPU texture instantiation.
testable_application: Inspect GLB textures first; if material textures dominate, A/B KTX2 transfer, transcode, VRAM, and scroll cadence.

evidence: Three KTX2Loader transcodes Basis Universal to a supported GPU format and requires renderer capability detection.
testable_application: Include transcoder/WASM cold cost and worker count in any KTX2 experiment.

evidence: decode() resolves when an image is decoded and safe to present without pausing the next frame.
testable_application: Decode the next poster before swapping it during scroll; measure cold decode and frame impact.

evidence: The sizes prop enables a width-based srcset; preload is intended for the actual above-fold LCP image.
testable_application: Use correct sizes and one LCP preload; compare bytes and decode time at 430 px.

evidence: React Three Fiber supports demand rendering when scene state is static.
testable_application: A/B always versus hybrid active/demand rendering; check resume hitch and idle power.

evidence: Renderer info exposes draw calls and memory-related geometry, texture, and program counts.
testable_application: Log once after cold ready and at each story beat; avoid perturbing every frame.

evidence: Device memory is a rounded capability hint and explicitly supports conditional feature selection.
testable_application: Choose a conservative initial tier; promote/demote using measured cadence with hysteresis.

evidence: DPR maps CSS pixels to physical backing pixels and often exceeds 2 on mobile.
testable_application: Log CSS and backing dimensions; A/B 2.0, 1.5, and 1.25 caps.

evidence: Objective image metrics correlated with perceived quality when validated against controlled subjective paired comparisons.
testable_application: Use objective crops and timing to narrow candidates, then make the promotion decision with a stated paired visual question.

evidence: The official tech-spec section lists 15 motors, 25 cm height, 800 g mass, camera plus LiDAR and two IMUs, seven trained moves, and a 50 Hz onboard policy loop.
testable_application: Use only these verified values in the website specification row.

evidence: The control loop reads 15 servos plus the imu_to_dxl device, decides 15 joint targets, and writes them at 50 Hz.
testable_application: Explain the simulator's 14-element body pose array as excluding the separate beak actuator; retain the official 15-motor product claim.

evidence: Document scroll events and requestAnimationFrame callbacks fire at approximately the same rate, so rAF is not a meaningful scroll-event throttling mechanism by itself.
testable_application: Use the existing frame authority for coalesced state sampling; measure target-versus-actual progress phase lag before adding another rAF boundary.

evidence: SwiftShader implements Vulkan/OpenGL ES on the CPU; Chromium can exercise GPU code paths while actually running software rendering.
testable_application: Treat SwiftShader traces as deterministic software-raster diagnostics, not evidence of hardware-GPU or physical-device throughput.

evidence: compileAsync compiles scene materials to avoid first-use shader compilation stutter, but its contract is compilation rather than presentation of a full visible frame.
testable_application: Gate ready on a representative presented frame in addition to compileAsync; test reveal and resize separately.

evidence: An image's natural width and height are density-corrected presentation dimensions; the standard explicitly divides intrinsic dimensions by current pixel density.
testable_application: Use source-file physical dimensions for decoded-memory budgeting, not density-corrected naturalWidth/naturalHeight.

evidence: InstancedMesh renders many objects that share geometry and material with different world transforms, reducing draw calls; changed instance matrices must be marked for update.
testable_application: Instance only repeated rigid parts with identical geometry and material, drive matrices from the existing rig, then measure calls, matrix-update CPU, cadence, and story-beat image parity.

evidence: Cycles baking requires a mesh UV map and an active image target; Diffuse with only Color selected captures surface color without direct or indirect lighting, tangent normals are suitable for animated objects, and island margins prevent mip/filter seams.
testable_application: Bake material color rather than studio lighting into mesh-space UVs, keep tangent normals optional, and inspect articulated parts plus mip seams.

evidence: Blender's glTF exporter recognizes image textures connected to Principled Base Color and the glTF metallic-roughness packing convention, with roughness in green and metallic in blue as non-color data.
testable_application: Replace unsupported procedural branches with baked base-color and packed metallic-roughness images before export; validate the exported material graph rather than assuming automatic bake.

evidence: glTF base-color textures are sRGB, metallic-roughness uses linear green/blue channels, and texture bindings reference mesh texture coordinates; factors multiply sampled texture values.
testable_application: Lock mesh UVs and color-space annotations, then share scalar factors or masks only where the glTF material model can express them.

evidence: Three textures containing color data require an sRGB or linear-sRGB annotation, while texture sampling/filtering, anisotropy, and disposal remain explicit runtime concerns.
testable_application: Mark baked base color as sRGB, keep roughness/metal/normal data in no-color space, and compare the calibrated handoff under the same renderer output transform.

evidence: Blender Average Island Scale makes UV islands approximately equal in scale; Minimize Stretch reduces angular distortion.
testable_application: Normalize texel density before packing the robot atlas, then allocate extra area only to the lens/head graphics justified by screen-space review.

evidence: Roughness controls microfacet reflection width; metallic 1 removes diffuse and uses tinted specular reflection.
testable_application: Lock lights and A/B hardware metallic 1 with bounded roughness variation against the prior mixed-metal value.

evidence: Light linking restricts receivers and is most efficient with the light tree; it may increase sampling complexity.
testable_application: Restrict the eye light to the lens and compare spill, noise, and render time.

evidence: Adaptive sampling stops converged pixels by noise threshold; lower thresholds increase quality and time.
testable_application: A/B fixed 128 samples against a high cap with explicit noise threshold; inspect stone pores, lens, and dark mechanisms.

evidence: Albedo and normal auxiliary passes help denoising preserve edges, textures, and fine detail.
testable_application: Save noisy plus auxiliary-pass denoise and inspect pigment lettering, wear, and pores at 1:1.

evidence: Light groups produce per-light combined passes that can be recombined without rerendering.
testable_application: Use light-group A/B to tune key/fill/rim influence without confounding material edits.

evidence: AgX provides wide dynamic range and desaturates high exposures.
testable_application: Lock AgX and exposure during material A/B; change exposure only in a dedicated lighting experiment.

evidence: getPointAt maps normalized distance to curve parameter; getPoint uses the raw curve parameter. Arc-length caches need updating after control points change.
testable_application: Sample the camera path by normalized arc length, then deliberately ease story phases; audit screen-space velocity because constant world speed does not imply constant projected speed.

evidence: CatmullRomCurve3 interpolates 3D control points and defaults to the centripetal variant.
testable_application: Author the hero angle and departure as one path with stable control points; check between checkpoints for overshoot and framing loss.

evidence: Three expects normalized quaternions and provides spherical interpolation between endpoint rotations.
testable_application: Derive camera orientation from the same progress as translation; check quaternion angular deltas and screen-space look-target continuity.

evidence: The example places images at different z coordinates and derives zoom and grayscale ranges through useScroll within one ScrollControls tree. It demonstrates shared progress and depth placement, not the requested robot landing or a physical-set camera path.
testable_application: Reuse one-progress ownership and depth separation; replace example image cards with the real authored set meshes.

evidence: Depth-ordering experiments found complementary relative-motion and accretion/deletion contributions, with cue utility varying across simulated depth differences.
testable_application: Keep near podium, robot, bench and far banner at distinct depths; compare their projected motion and occluding edges while the camera moves. This website application is an inference.

evidence: Random-dot experiments examined dynamic occlusion and motion parallax with moving observers and with surfaces moving relative to stationary observers.
testable_application: Compare actual geometric parallax against a translated flat poster as a falsification control; the study does not prescribe this website camera path.

evidence: In 72 four-month-old infants, changing both shape and color behind an occluder affected trajectory continuity judgments. This developmental result is adjacent evidence, not direct adult website validation.
testable_application: Preserve the same robot geometry, paint, and continuous trajectory through set departure, then test reverse-scroll identity in local captures.

evidence: Launching judgments were sensitive to contact delay, but several classical delay predictions did not replicate. The study does not establish a universal threshold for UI animation.
testable_application: Implement the user-selected contact-to-explode order without a separate dwell interval; test that explode is zero before touchdown and grows immediately after the shared phase boundary.

evidence: The documented one-frame contact-shadow optimization applies when objects are static; the effect is otherwise described as expensive.
testable_application: Keep contact cues consistent with the moving feet through takeoff and landing. A frozen frames=1 shadow requires a static caster or a separately validated analytic shadow.

evidence: Nonessential interaction-driven animation, including parallax, can trigger vestibular symptoms; the guidance describes disabling motion and respecting a reduced-motion preference.
testable_application: Provide a static readable reduced-motion presentation with the same product information, rather than forcing the jump and traveling camera.

concept: portable scene nodes and PBR maps
evidence: glTF stores scene nodes and mesh primitives; texture bindings select mesh coordinates. Base-color data uses sRGB, while packed roughness green and metallic blue use linear transfer.
testable_application: Export real authored set geometry with UV-bound materials; inspect node bounds, texture channels, draw calls and texture dimensions instead of substituting a whole-scene image card.

evidence: The exporter documents meshes, materials, textures, cameras and punctual point, spot and directional lights. This supported list does not promise transfer of Blender World or area-light rigs.
testable_application: Bake procedural surface channels to UV images, recreate runtime light/environment intent explicitly, and compare the white/cobalt/dark hero against Blender before judging the departure.

concept: lossless geometry transport and float entropy
evidence: EXT_meshopt_compression independently compresses buffer views; NONE filtering can retain exact vertex/index bytes. Further gzip effectiveness depends on the resulting entropy and must be measured.
testable_application: Compare plain GLB gzip with meshopt plus gzip, reject quantization, and byte-compare every decoded view before adopting.
local_validation: tested-fail: 75 views / 9209280 bytes decode identically, but meshopt+gzip is 7991460 bytes versus plain gzip 7492826. Keep plain gzip.
